insights.headline: Weekly wrap: gold and silver fell through the week on hot US CPI and Fed rate-hike bets
insights.summary: The week's data shows a broad retreat: IBJA figures put 24-carat gold down ₹3,004 to ₹1,46,426 per 10 grams and silver down ₹10,191 to ₹2,10,918 per kg, with spot gold near $4,186 and silver near $57. September's hot US CPI revived bets on a Fed rate hike, lifting yields and the dollar, while Brent crude held above $110 on supply concerns. Policy stayed active: SEBI's gold-fund subscription curbs and the RBI's ₹14,614 premature redemption price for SGB 2020-21 Series VII. As Dhanteras nears, a Mint column urges buyers to treat festive gold as ritual rather than investment.
points: Hot US CPI revived Fed rate-hike bets; gold fell 0.5% on the week to $4,177.82, silver slid 5.3% before a Friday rebound
Brent held above $110/bbl, first time since May, on supply concerns
SEBI's gold FoF curbs may have limited impact with the ETF route open; RBI set SGB Series VII exit price at ₹14,614
Mint: Dhanteras gold buying is ritual, not investing — making charges and locker costs erode returns

trending.title: Rate-hike fears cap the metals’ recovery
trending.summary: Hot September US CPI revived Fed tightening bets, pressuring gold and silver through the week; a softer dollar and lower yields aided Friday's partial rebound.

trending.title: Policy acts on gold demand ahead of Diwali
trending.summary: Fund houses halted fresh gold FoF subscriptions ahead of the festive season to curb imports, while the ETF route stays open; RBI fixed the SGB Series VII exit price at Rs 14,614.

trending.title: Silver’s steep slide flashes an economic warning
trending.summary: Silver is down more than 50% from its January record high of $121.79 to around $57; its monetary-plus-industrial role makes the slide a possible economic warning.

trending.title: Dhanteras: ritual buying meets high prices
trending.summary: A Mint column says treat Dhanteras gold as ritual, not investing, since making charges and locker costs eat returns; IBJA's weekly numbers show softer prices ahead of the festival.

trending.title: India’s import picture is shifting
trending.summary: Gold imports plunged 81% to a 30-month low on higher duties and weaker demand, while central banks bought a record 288.9 tonnes in Q2; domestic supply pressure is easing.

items.title: Gold Falls ₹3,000 This Week, Silver Slides Over ₹10,000
items.summary: IBJA data showed 24-carat gold falling ₹3,004 over the week to ₹1,46,426 per 10 grams and silver sliding ₹10,191 to ₹2,10,918 per kg; spot gold traded near $4,186 and silver near $57 as rising crude lifted the dollar.

items.title: SEBI's gold fund curbs may have limited impact as ETF route remains open
items.summary: SEBI has directed mutual funds to bar fresh lump-sum investments, new SIPs and STPs into gold ETF fund-of-funds from October 16, and about 17 fund houses have complied. Redemptions and existing SIP instalments continue, and direct gold ETFs stay buyable on exchanges — a gap experts say could blunt the curbs. The move aims to ease pressure on the rupee and the gold import bill.

items.title: Weekly Bullion Review: Gold Falls 0.5% to $4,177.82 as Hot US CPI Revives Fed Rate Hike Bets; Silver Tumbles 5.3% Before Friday Rebound
items.summary: Gold slipped 0.5% on the week to $4,177.82 after September US CPI came in hot at 3.7% year-on-year, reviving bets on a Fed rate hike. Silver fared worse, plunging 5.3% over the week before a Friday rebound to $57.86. On MCX, December gold settled near Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 grams and December silver near Rs 2.13 lakh per kg.

items.title: RBI fixes SGB 2020-21 Series VII premature redemption price at Rs 14,614; exit window on October 19
items.summary: The RBI fixed the premature redemption price of Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at Rs 14,614 per unit — about a 192% capital gain for digital subscribers who paid Rs 5,001 in October 2020. The exit window was moved to October 19 because October 20 is a Dussehra holiday. Holders can also stay until the October 2028 maturity and keep collecting 2.5% annual interest.

items.title: Brent crude hits $110 a barrel for first time since May as supply concerns mount
items.summary: Brent crude touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May on October 17 as Iran-related supply fears intensified, before easing back toward $105. Costlier oil lifts inflation expectations and US yields — a headwind for gold — and pressures the rupee, which raises the landed cost of gold in India.

items.title: Bullion Cues: Weakness may deepen
items.summary: Gold ($4,165.40) and silver ($57) lost 0.7% and 6.3% last week; MCX gold futures (₹1,47,918) fell 2.4% and silver (₹2,11,187) 6.5%. The Hindu BusinessLine's research bureau says MCX gold must cross ₹1,51,700 to turn positive, with supports at ₹1,43,500 and ₹1,41,000; silver could slide to the ₹2,00,000–2,00,750 band unless it reclaims ₹2,28,000–2,30,000.

items.title: Gold's Split Screen: Sticky Inflation on One Side, Central-Bank Buying on the Other
items.summary: Gold closed the session at $4,169.08, holding near weekly support after Thursday's rebound: a softer dollar and falling Treasury yields offset the September CPI shock (3.7% headline, 2.6% core) that firmed October hike bets. Speculators had already trimmed net-long positions before the data landed, while steady central-bank buying continues to cushion the downside.

items.title: Silver's recent 50% drop from a record high hints that an economic slowdown looms
items.summary: Silver futures touched a record intraday $121.79 an ounce in late January, per Dow Jones Market Data, and have since lost more than half, settling at $57.31 on Friday. Dealers told MarketWatch that silver's dual monetary-industrial role makes its weakness a leading indicator of economic trouble as high energy prices bite. Gold has fallen more than 25% from its own January record of $5,626.80.

items.title: Gold imports plunge 81% to 30-month low; ICRA sees CAD widening to 0.9% of GDP
items.summary: India's gold imports plunged 81.3% year-on-year to $1.8 billion in September — the lowest in 30 months — helping narrow the merchandise trade deficit to $30.2 billion from $33 billion, Commerce Ministry data showed. The $7.8 billion drop in the gold bill more than offset higher oil and electronics imports. ICRA said the easing was non-oil driven and forecast the CAD at 0.9% of GDP in FY27.

items.title: [SMM Analysis] Silver Down Nearly 20% From Stage High: Why Are Solar Cell Prices Not Following?
items.summary: SMM's #1 silver price fell 19.6% from its August 27 high of 16,889 yuan/kg to 13,584 yuan/kg on October 15, edging to 13,842 yuan/kg on the 16th. Yet solar cell prices barely budged: M10 cell costs fell 10.8% to 0.310 yuan/W while G12R prices held flat since September 18. SMM blames hawkish Fed minutes, a dollar index above 102 and multi-year-high yields; COMEX silver broke below $60 on October 8.

items.title: Gold on Dhanteras: celebrate the ritual, rethink the investment
items.summary: A Mint column argues Dhanteras gold buying should be treated as ritual rather than investing: jewellery's making charges vanish on resale and coins sit in rented lockers, making festive gold consumption rather than a financial plan.

items.title: India Bullion: Up on weak dollar; market assesses Fed rate outlook
items.summary: MCX December gold rose 0.6% to ₹1,48,320 per 10 grams and December silver gained 1.4% to ₹2,13,570 per kg on Friday as the dollar index fell to a two-week low of 101.57; COMEX gold was up 0.6% at $4,195.3 and silver up 1.5% at $57.99. Kotak Securities cited safe-haven flows from the equity selloff, while Commerzbank said Fed Chair Warsh's comments further dented October hike expectations.

items.title: Sensex gains 414 points; MCX gold up 0.64% to Rs 1,48,429, silver up 1.33% to Rs 2,13,460 on Friday
items.summary: MCX bullion futures rebounded on Friday: December gold rose 0.64% to Rs 1,48,429 per 10 grams and December silver gained 1.33% to Rs 2,13,460 per kg, after a weak week. The bounce tracked softer US bond yields and a weaker dollar, though the rupee's gains capped the domestic move. Brent eased to about $105 after touching $110.

items.title: Selling Pressure Resumption Could Push Gold To US$4,000, Says RHB
items.summary: RHB Research kept its bearish call on COMEX gold despite Thursday's rebound to a $4,170.10 close, calling it a countertrend bounce with the RSI still below 50. The house advises holding shorts initiated September 23 at $4,284.80 with a $4,400 stop-loss; a failure to clear $4,200 resistance could renew selling toward $4,000 and then $3,800. RHB stays negative unless gold moves above $4,400.
